summary: On June 3, 1999, a peace agreement was finally signed that represented a compromise between the Rambouillet accord that Yugoslavia had rejected and the Serbian National Assembly's proposal that had never been seriously considered. Noam Chomsky concluded that diplomatic initiatives could have averted the human tragedy.

citation.quote: When a peace agreement was finally signed on June 3, 1999, it was a compromise between the Rambouillet accord, which Yugoslavia had rejected, and the Serbian National Assembly proposal, which had never been seriously considered.

title: Eight pacifists arrested blocking traffic to nuclear submarine base in Bangor, Maine; acquitted by jury
summary: On the anniversary of the bombing of Nagasaki in August 1999, eight pacifists blocked four lanes of traffic leading to a nuclear submarine base in Bangor, Maine, housing eight Trident submarines with over a thousand nuclear warheads. They were arrested but ultimately acquitted by the jury.

citation.quote: On the anniversary of the bombing of Nagasaki in August 1999, eight pacifists decided to block four lanes of traffic leading to a nuclear submarine base in Bangor, Maine. At that base, eight Trident submarines were housed, carrying over a thousand nuclear warheads. The protesters were arrested.

title: 40,000-person labor march and farmer rally at WTO protests in Seattle
summary: On November 30, 1999, farmers joined a huge AFL-CIO labor march of 40,000 people at the Seattle WTO protests, with union people then attending a family farm rally a few days later in an unprecedented North-South solidarity.

citation.quote: Farmers joined a huge labor march of 40,000 on November 30, and then union people attended a family farm rally a few days later.

title: US sold over $11 billion of arms in 1999, one-third of all weapons sold worldwide
summary: In the summer of 2000, the New York Times reported that in 1999 the United States had sold over $11 billion of arms, representing one-third of all weapons sold worldwide, two-thirds of which went to poor countries.

citation.quote: In the summer of 2000, the New York Times reported that in the previous year the United States had sold over $11 billion of arms, one-third of all weapons sold worldwide.

title: Biggest white-collar strike in US history won by 19,000 Boeing engineers
summary: In the year 2000, the biggest white-collar strike in the nation's history was won by 19,000 engineers and professional workers of Boeing, who succeeded in having their salaries match those of workers in other Boeing plants.

citation.quote: In the year 2000, the biggest white-collar strike in the nation's history was won for 19,000 engineers and professional workers of Boeing, who succeeded in having their salaries match those of workers in other Boeing plants.

title: Congress passes resolution authorizing military action without a declaration of war
summary: In response to the September 11 attacks, Congress passed a resolution giving Bush power to proceed with military action, bypassing the constitutional requirement for a formal declaration of war. The resolution passed unanimously in the Senate; only Barbara Lee dissented in the House.

citation.chapter: Chapter 25 – The 2000 Election and the "War on Terrorism"
citation.quote: Congress rushed to pass resolutions giving Bush the power to proceed with military action, without the declaration of war that the Constitution required. The resolution passed unanimously in the Senate, and in the House of Representatives only one member dissented—Barbara Lee, an African American from California.

title: September 11 attacks on World Trade Center and Pentagon
summary: Nineteen hijackers flew fuel-laden jets into the twin towers of the World Trade Center in New York and into the Pentagon in Washington, D.C., killing thousands of workers, firefighters, and police. The attacks were described as an unprecedented assault on symbols of American wealth and power.
location: New York, New York; Washington, D.C.

citation.chapter: Chapter 25 – The 2000 Election and the "War on Terrorism"
citation.quote: Nine months into his presidency, on September 11, 2001, a cataclysmic event pushed all other issues into the background. Hijackers on three different planes flew the huge jets, loaded with fuel, into the twin towers of the World Trade Center in downtown New York, and into one side of the Pentagon in Washington, D.C.

title: Bush orders bombing of Afghanistan
summary: Acting on the supposition that Osama bin Laden was responsible for the September 11 attacks and was hiding in Afghanistan, President Bush ordered the bombing of that country. The campaign killed at least 1,000 and perhaps 4,000 Afghan civilians according to human rights groups.

citation.chapter: Chapter 25 – The 2000 Election and the "War on Terrorism"
citation.quote: On the supposition that the Islamic militant Osama bin Laden was responsible for the September 11 attacks, and that he was somewhere in Afghanistan, Bush ordered the bombing of Afghanistan.

title: New York Times editorializes praising Bush as strong wartime leader
summary: Despite having opposed Bush in the 2000 election, the New York Times editorialized in December 2001 that Bush had proved himself a strong wartime leader who gave the nation a sense of security during a crisis.

citation.chapter: Chapter 25 – The 2000 Election and the "War on Terrorism"
citation.quote: The New York Times, which had opposed Bush in the election, editorialized in December 2001: "Mr. Bush . . . has proved himself a strong wartime leader who gives the nation a sense of security during a period of crisis."

title: Families of 9/11 victims travel to Afghanistan to meet Afghan families
summary: Family members of those killed in the World Trade Center and Pentagon attacks traveled to Afghanistan in January 2002 to meet Afghan families who had lost loved ones in American bombing raids, including Rita Lasar, whose brother was cited as a hero by President Bush.

citation.chapter: Chapter 25 – The 2000 Election and the "War on Terrorism"
citation.quote: Some of the families of victims traveled to Afghanistan in January 2002, to meet with Afghan families who had lost loved ones in the American bombing.
